unreleased.text: Help ▸ BoopStash Help shows what the app does and how it treats your notes, without going online.
Settings ▸ Help shows what the app does and how it treats your notes, without going online.
What's New: after an update, BoopStash shows once what changed. The notes stay in Help ▸ What's New and in Settings, and can be copied or saved as a note.
What's New: after an update, BoopStash shows once what changed. The notes stay in Settings ▸ What's New, and can be copied or saved as a note.
Clean Up Pasted Text in the Edit menu tidies text copied from a terminal: tables become Markdown tables, and shared indentation, trailing spaces and colour codes go.
Copy Text from Image: right-click an image in the editor to copy the text in it, or to insert that text below the image.
Touch and hold an image in a note's preview to copy the text in it.
Text read from images keeps its rows, so a screenshot of a table pastes into a spreadsheet as a table.
Letting go of the preview divider where you grabbed it no longer changes the split.

notes.text: Window ▸ BoopStash (⌘0) brings the main window back after it is closed; New Note opens it too.

Find and replace in a note, as in VS Code: ⌘F opens a widget with Match Case, Whole Word and Regular Expression toggles and the match count; ⌥⌘F unfolds the replace row; Enter and ⇧Enter step through the matches; $1 works in regular expression replacements.
With iCloud sync on, a note edited soon after its first sync is no longer emptied into a "(conflict)" copy.
With iCloud sync on, an edit made soon after a note first synced could end up in a "(conflict)" copy; it now stays in the note.
The note list no longer stays on an old filter when the filter changes twice in quick succession.
BoopStash ▸ Install Command Line Tool… puts the boopstash command on your PATH, for copies not installed with Homebrew.
The preview beside the editor keeps the size you drag it to, across notes and relaunches.
With the preview on, every note you open renders, not just the first.
Labels: put coloured labels on notes, see them as chips in the list, and filter by them. Settings ▸ Labels makes, renames and recolours them.
Labels made on your Mac show as coloured chips, and the Filter menu lists only the notes carrying the labels you check.
Report a Problem in the Help menu makes a note describing the app and what is on screen, with an optional screenshot of the window, ready to copy into an issue.
The editor shows its text again: the folding gutter no longer paints over the note.
Search by meaning: a search also finds notes that say the same thing in other words, using a small language model on your Mac. Show Similar Notes lists a note's closest neighbours.
Search by meaning: a search also finds notes that say the same thing in other words, using a small language model on your device. Show Similar Notes lists a note's closest neighbours.
Notes shared from other apps are found by meaning too.
Folding: fold code blocks, JSON, XML and HTML elements and Markdown sections from the gutter or the Edit menu.
A boopstash command for the terminal: pipe output into a note, and list, search and show notes, with JSON output.
Format Document for Python, Go, shell, C, C++ and Java.
The language menu shows the language in use; the toolbar has Paste as Markdown, Run Script and the previews.
The preview is for Markdown notes; XML formatting keeps text exactly; long notes with many images scroll smoothly.

iCloud sync, off until you turn it on in Settings: your notes and images stay the same on every Mac, iPhone and iPad signed in to your Apple Account, encrypted on your device before they are uploaded.
BoopStash for iPhone and iPad: the same notes and search, syntax highlighting, light editing and the Markdown preview.
Share to BoopStash: share text, a link or up to ten images from any app and they become a note.
BoopStash is on the Mac App Store as well as Homebrew.
Images: paste or drop an image into a note. Each shows as a chip with a thumbnail, and export writes images beside the notes.
Text in images is searchable, read on your Mac by Apple's text recognition.
Markdown preview: View ▸ Show Preview (⌥⌘P) renders the note beside the editor or in its place, and never loads anything.
Format Document for JSON, XML, JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, YAML, Markdown and SQL.
Boop scripts: Scripts ▸ Run Script… (⌘B) runs Boop's scripts on the selection or the whole note, and your own from the Scripts folder.
The app is now spelled BoopStash and has its own icon; your notes and settings carry over.
Settings ▸ Editor: the editor's font and size, and a theme each for light and dark appearance.
Fixes for line commands on Windows line endings, links in Paste as Markdown, dropped files and titles.
The first release: a scratch pad for macOS that keeps what you paste, with notes that name themselves and a filter that matches inside words.
An editor that leaves your text alone, with VS Code, JetBrains or Emacs key bindings and syntax highlighting for twenty languages.
Capture from the clipboard with ⌥⌘N, with ⌃⌥⌘V from any app, or with Services ▸ Save to BoopStash.
